observations: Photo 0 shows a close-up of a worn, white-painted metal machine with peeling paint, a green control panel with colorful stitch patterns, a yellow knob, and a metal lever.
Photo 1 shows a similar view from a slightly different angle, revealing a small black label with 'BUTTERFLY' written vertically in white letters on the left side of the control panel.
The machine appears to be an industrial sewing machine, likely a double-needle model given the 'double' in the seller's description and the presence of two needle positions on the panel.
The control panel has a grid of 60 stitch patterns (numbered 1-60) with color-coded symbols, suggesting it is a multi-stitch industrial machine.
The machine is visibly aged, with rust, chipped paint, and dirt. No machine stand is visible, consistent with the seller's note.
No power cord, motor, or foot pedal is visible in either photo.

claims.evidence: Photo 1 shows the 'BUTTERFLY' brand name on a label, and the machine's design with dual needle positions and a multi-stitch panel supports 'double industrial machine'.
Neither photo shows a stand; the machine is resting on a surface, and the seller explicitly notes its absence.

risks.risk: Machine may not be functional (e.g., motor, electrical components, or mechanical parts may be broken or missing).
risks.proof: A video showing the machine powered on, with the needle moving and the motor running, or a photo of the motor and power cord.

risks.risk: Missing critical parts (e.g., foot pedal, power cord, or needle bar assembly).
risks.proof: A full view of the machine from all angles, including the underside and rear, showing all components.

risks.risk: Severe wear or damage affecting usability (e.g., rusted gears, broken levers, or damaged control panel).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the internal mechanisms, gears, and electrical connections.

proof_requests: Video of the machine operating (motor running, needle moving).
Photos of the motor, power cord, and foot pedal (if any).
Full 360-degree photos showing all sides and components.
response.reason: The brand and type are identifiable, but critical functional and completeness risks remain unverified. Without proof of working condition and full component set, the item cannot be priced accurately.
